verses.zh: 犹大王约沙法平平安安地回耶路撒冷，到宫里去了。
verses.en: When King Jehoshaphat of Judah returned home safely to Jerusalem,[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
19:1-11 This material is unique to Chronicles and, as usual, comes from a written prophetic source (i.e., 2 Chr. 21:34).

19:1 "returned" This VERB (BDB 996, KB 1427, Qal IMPERFECT with
waw) is often used of repentance. One wonders if it functions both

- physically ‒ the king escaped the battle and came back to Jerusalem

- spiritually ‒ the king recognized his folly and came back to faith in YHWH/li>

This same VERB occurs in verse 4, "brought them back to the Lord."

verses.zh: 先见哈拿尼的儿子耶户出来迎接约沙法王，对他说：「你岂当帮助恶人，爱那恨恶耶和华的人呢？因此耶和华的忿怒临到你。
verses.en: the prophet[NOTE:1] Jehu son of Hanani confronted him;[NOTE:2] he said to King Jehoshaphat, “Is it right to help the wicked and be an ally of those who oppose the Lord?[NOTE:3] Because you have done this, the Lord is angry with you![NOTE:4]
notes: Or “seer.”
Heb “went out to his face.”
Heb “and love those who hate the Lord?”
Heb “and because of this upon you is anger from before the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
19:2 "Jehu the son of Hanani" This prophet's father, Hanani, had addressed King Asa earlier in 2 Chr. 16:7. Jehu's
written account of Jehoshaphat is the Chronicler's written source (cf. 2 Chr. 20:34).

Jehu asks the king a series of ironical questions.

- why help the wicked?

- why love those who hate the Lord?

- why bring YHWH's wrath on yourself?

There is some confusion between Kings and Chronicles on the name of the prophet.

- 1 Kgs. 16:1,7 ‒ Jehu son of Hanani

- 2 Chr. 16:7 ‒ Hanani the seer

Possibly both father and son addressed Baasha; if so, he had moved from the northern kingdom to Judah.

"the seer" This is one of several names for prophets.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE DIFFERENT HEBREW TERMS FOR PROPHET

"those who hate" This VERB (BDB 971, KB 1338, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPLE)
is used

- in the "Ten Commandments" (cf. Exod. 20:5; Deut. 5:9)

- of YHWH's enemies in Num. 10:35; Ps. 68:1; 139:21

- of false followers in Ps. 81:15; 83:2

- in the powerful comparison of love and hate in Deut. 7:9-11; love is obedience and hate is disobedience (usually idolatry)

verses.zh: 然而你还有善行，因你从国中除掉木偶，立定心意寻求　神。
verses.en: Nevertheless you have done some good things;[NOTE:1] you removed[NOTE:2] the Asherah poles from the land, and you were determined to follow God.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “nevertheless good things are found with you.”
Here בָּעַר (baʿar) is not the well attested verb “burn,” but the less common homonym meaning “devastate, sweep away, remove.” See HALOT 146 s.v. II בער.
Heb “and you set your heart to seek God.”
verses.commentary:
19:3 The spiritual condition of Jehoshaphat is so different between 1 Kings 22 (i.e., 1 Kgs. 22:4b) and 2 Chronicles
17-20 (i.e., 2 Chr. 19:3a, "there is some good in you"). The Chronicler used Jehoshaphat as an example of a godly king, with
some faults and mistakes. Jehoshaphat is used to highlight some of the Chronicler's theological themes directed to the post-exilic
Judean community.

- faith in YHWH (seek Him with all your heart)

- obedience to His law

- need for repentance

- blessing for covenant obedience and cursing for disobedience (i.e., Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28)

YHWH will restore Jehoshaphat because

- he removed (or tried to remove) the local Ba'al sites called "high places"; those fertility worshipers sought a
topologically high place (hill) or built a stone platform (cf. 2 Chr. 17:6)

- he set his heart to seek YHWH (cf. 2 Chr. 17:6, which is the opposite of 2 Chr. 12:14); for "seek" see note at 2 Chr. 7:14

verses.zh: 约沙法住在耶路撒冷，以后又出巡民间，从别是巴直到以法莲山地，引导民归向耶和华―他们列祖的　神；
verses.en: Jehoshaphat lived in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1] He went out among the people from Beer Sheba to the hill country of Ephraim and encouraged them to follow[NOTE:2] the Lord God of their ancestors.[NOTE:3]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “and turned them back to.”
Heb “fathers.”
verses.commentary:
19:4-6 These verses describe the religious activities of Jehoshaphat in his attempt to improve the spiritual sensitivity
of Judah.

- he personally traveled his whole country promoting the worship of YHWH alone, 2 Chr. 19:4

- he appointed judges who would only consider the revealed covenant guidelines from YHWH, 2 Chr. 19:6-7; this may be
what is mentioned in 2 Chr. 17:7-9 (see NIDOTTE, vol. 4, pp. 213-220)

- he instructed the judges to fear the Lord

- judge in righteousness

- do not show favoritism

- do not take a bribe (i.e., Deut. 1:17; Ps. 15:5)

- his final admonition is in 2 Chr. 19:11 ‒ "be strong and do" (two Qal IMPERATIVES)

These (i.e., a - d) reflect YHWH's character (cf. Deut. 10:17-18; 32:4).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

19:4 "to the hill country of Ephraim" This implies that Judah had influence far north of their border.

verses.zh: 又在犹大国中遍地的坚固城里设立审判官，
verses.en: He appointed judges throughout the land and in each of the fortified cities of Judah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “in the land in all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city.”

verses.zh: 对他们说：「你们办事应当谨慎；因为你们判断不是为人，乃是为耶和华。判断的时候，他必与你们同在。
verses.en: He told the judges, “Be careful what you do,[NOTE:1] for you are not judging for men, but for the Lord, who will be with you when you make judicial decisions.
notes: Heb “see what you are doing.”

verses.zh: 现在你们应当敬畏耶和华，谨慎办事；因为耶和华―我们的　神没有不义，不偏待人，也不受贿赂。」
verses.en: Respect the Lord and make careful decisions, for the Lord our God disapproves of injustice, partiality, and bribery.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and now let the terror of the Lord be upon you, be careful and act for there is not with the Lord our God injustice, lifting up of a face, and taking a bribe.”
verses.commentary:
19:7 "let the fear of the Lord be upon you" This is a JUSSIVE of the "to be"
VERB (BDB 224, KB 243).

There is a theological distinction between

- the fear of YHWH's people for their God (i.e., "awe," "respect," cf. 2 Chr. 19:9)

- "the dread" (BDB 808) is a "holy" term

- the exodus ‒ Exod. 15:14-16; 23:27

- the wilderness wanderings ‒ Deut. 2:25

- the conquest ‒ Josh. 2:9

- David ‒ 1 Chr. 14:17

- Asa ‒ 2 Chr. 14:13

- Jehoshaphat ‒ 2 Chr. 17:10; 20:29

One wonders why Jehoshaphat instigated these judicial reforms.

- he saw the corruption in the north

- he recognized the corruption in areas of his kingdom

- he wanted to show the priority of YHWH's covenant and law

- it was a way to show his repentance

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR

verses.zh: 约沙法从利未人和祭司，并以色列族长中派定人，在耶路撒冷为耶和华判断，听民间的争讼，就回耶路撒冷去了。
verses.en: In Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appointed some Levites, priests, and Israelite family leaders to judge on behalf of the Lord[NOTE:1] and to settle disputes among the residents of Jerusalem.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for the judgment of the Lord.”

Heb “and to conduct a case [or “for controversy”], and they returned [to] Jerusalem.” Some emend וַיָּשֻׁבוּ (vayyashuvu, “and they returned”) to וַיֵּשְׁבוּ (vayyeshevu, “and they lived [in]”). The present translation assumes an emendation to יֹשְׁבֵי (yoshevey, “residents of”).
verses.commentary:
19:8-11 Jehoshaphat also appointed judges in Jerusalem.

- Levites

- priests

- heads of families

Some dealt with covenant issues, family issues (2 Chr. 19:10), and some more practical royal issues (v. 11).

As he gave guidelines for the judges throughout Judah, so too, for Jerusalem.

- judge in fear/awe of the Lord, v. 9

- judge faithfully (i.e., to the covenant guidelines), v. 9

- judge wholeheartedly (i.e., with complete devotion to YHWH and His covenant), v. 9

Jehoshaphat's action in appointing these "judges" may go back to Deut. 1:16-17; 16:18-20; 17:8-13 and set the
precedent for the Sanhedrin in Ezra's day.

If there was a difficult case somewhere in the nation that could not be decided, it should be brought to the higher
court in Jerusalem.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE SANHEDRIN

19:8 "Israel" In this context it refers to the descendants of Jacob who made up Judah.

verses.en: He commanded them: “Carry out your duties with respect for the Lord, with honesty, and with pure motives.[NOTE:1]

verses.zh: 住在各城里你们的弟兄，若有争讼的事来到你们这里，或为流血，或犯律法、诫命、律例、典章，你们要警戒他们，免得他们得罪耶和华，以致他的忿怒临到你们和你们的弟兄；这样行，你们就没有罪了。
verses.en: Whenever your countrymen who live in the cities bring a case before you[NOTE:1] (whether it involves a violent crime[NOTE:2] or other matters related to the law, commandments, rules, and regulations), warn them that they must not sin against the Lord. If you fail to do so, God will be angry with you and your colleagues, but if you obey, you will be free of guilt.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and every case which comes to you from your brothers who live in their cities.”
Heb “between blood pertaining to blood.”
Heb “and anger will be upon you and your brothers; do this and you will not be guilty.”

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR GOD'S REVELATION.

Notice the two things YHWH promises if the judges are faithful.

- you will not be guilty (i.e., the "they" is ambiguous and could refer to the people or the judge, 2 Chr. 19:10)

- the Lord will be with the upright (JUSSIVE)

- individually (the judges and those who seek YHWH)

- collectively Judah will be blessed (Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28)

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- How long did Jehu prophesy and where?

- List the ways Jehoshaphat showed allegiance to Ahab.

- List the things Jehoshaphat did that were "good." (v. 3)

- Why did Jehoshaphat appoint "new" judges?

- List how they should judge.

- Was there a supreme court in Jerusalem or a court of appeals?
